decisions.reason: The same two words open Genesis 1:1 in the Greek Old Testament. John is retelling creation, so every level keeps the echo.
Key term. In Genesis 1 God creates by speaking, so the rendering should keep the link to God speaking. "Reason" imports Greek philosophy John does not develop.
πρός with the accusative normally means "toward"; here it describes presence and relationship. Where a language's natural word is weaker, the note carries the fuller sense.

ὁ λόγος has the article, so it is the subject. θεός comes first without the article and says what the Word is, without making the Word the same person as "the God" just mentioned. "A god" would contradict John's insistence on one God; "divine" is weaker than the noun.
The imperfect ἦν (was, continuing) contrasts with ἐγένετο (came into being) in verses 3, 6 and 14. Readable makes the contrast explicit.

"La Palabra" shows the link to God's speech more plainly, but it is feminine: verse 2 would need "Esta", and the Word would be "she" until becoming a man in verse 14. "El Verbo" is masculine, is the traditional term (from the Latin Verbum), and keeps the pronouns natural. The glossary explains that it means "the Word". For review by a native speaker.

decisions.choice: era for being or identity; estaba for presence
decisions.reason: Spanish must split one Greek verb into ser and estar. "Era el Verbo" and "era Dios" say what he is; "estaba con Dios" says where he was. The Spanish imperfect also carries the continuing sense of ἦν that English Readable had to add with "already".

"La Parole" says "speech" more plainly and keeps the link to God speaking in Genesis 1, but it is feminine: verse 2 would read "Elle était au commencement" and the Word would be "elle" until becoming a man in verse 14. "Le Verbe" is masculine, is the traditional French term (from the Latin Verbum) and keeps the pronouns natural; its weakness is that "verbe" today is mostly a grammar word, so the glossary says it means "the Word". For review by a native speaker, as the Spanish "el Verbo" is.

"Auprès de" says presence beside a person, closer to the relational sense of the Greek preposition than the bare "avec"; "tourné vers" copies the preposition’s basic sense, which the meaning decision leaves to the note. French "être" covers both identity and presence, so unlike Spanish no split of the verb is needed, and the imperfect "était" already carries the continuing sense.

"Neno" is the ordinary word for a word and for God's word, so it keeps the link to God speaking in Genesis 1. It is a class 5 noun, which would make it "lilikuwa" (it was); because the Word is a person, it takes the personal agreement "alikuwa" (he was), as Swahili does for nouns naming living beings. For review by a native speaker.

decisions.choice: alikuwako for existence; alikuwa kwa (L) or pamoja na (B, R) for presence; alikuwa for identity
alternatives: alikuwa kwa Mungu at every level
decisions.reason: Swahili splits ἦν three ways: "alikuwako" says the Word existed, "alikuwa ... Mungu" says what he is, and the preposition says where he was. For πρὸς Literal keeps "kwa Mungu" (at God's side, towards God); Balanced and Readable say "pamoja na Mungu" (together with God), which a reader cannot mistake for "by God" or "to God". Readable adds "tayari" (already) where the English Readable adds "already".

decisions.choice: "말씀" (key term), with the subject honorific ("말씀이 계셨다", "하나님이셨다")
decisions.reason: "말씀" is the ordinary respectful word for speech and for God's word, so it keeps the link to God speaking in Genesis 1. Because the Word is a person and is God, the verbs take the honorific -시- ("계셨다", "이셨다") at every level; "있었다" would treat the Word as a thing.

decisions.choice: "하나님" for God, every level and the whole book
decisions.reason: "하나님" is the Protestant word most Korean readers use; "하느님" is the Catholic and Common Translation word. Settled for the whole Bible: Korean follows the Protestant tradition's names and terms (the founder's decision, October 2026; docs/korean-style.md).

"태초에" is the word Korean readers know from Genesis 1:1, so it carries the allusion the meaning note describes. Readable uses the plain native phrase "맨 처음에" (at the very beginning) and adds "이미" (already) as the English Readable adds "already".

decisions.choice: "Ngôi Lời" (key term for logos) at every level
decisions.reason: "Lời" alone reads as a thing (a word, a message); "Ngôi" is the word Vietnamese uses for a person of the Godhead, and John's Word is a person who is with God and is God. "Đạo" (the Way, the Teaching) is an older choice that loses the link with God speaking in Genesis 1.

decisions.choice: "Đức Chúa Trời" for God, in the Protestant tradition, every level
decisions.reason: Names and key terms follow the Protestant tradition that most Vietnamese Bible readers online know; Catholic readers say "Thiên Chúa" (and "Gio-an", "Đức Giê-su"). Settled for the whole Bible: Vietnamese follows the Protestant tradition's names and terms (the founder's decision, October 2026; docs/vietnamese-style.md).

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on every Spanish pronoun for God or Christ
alternatives: stressed pronouns only (él, mí, ti, sí, tú)
decisions.reason: Book-wide rule for John in Spanish, the same as in Mark (Mark 1:2) and the rest of the Spanish New Testament: every pronoun Spanish writes for God or Christ takes the deity_pronoun setting, whether stressed (él, mí, ti, sí, tú), possessive (su, sus, mi, mis, tu, tus, mío, suyo) or an object pronoun standing before the verb (lo, le, me, te, and "se" where it stands for "le"). A subject that Spanish leaves in the verb ending has no pronoun to span. Written plain: a pronoun at the start of a sentence or quotation, as English writes "He"; a pronoun joined to the end of a verb ("sígueme", "matarlo"), which cannot take the capital; "conmigo" and "contigo"; and reflexives ("se sentó"). Pronouns for the Spirit follow the same rule, as in English. Pronouns for anyone else take no span: figures inside a picture, such as the bridegroom of 3:29 and the shepherd of 10:1-5, and the speaker's own "mi" and "mío" in "mi Señor" (Mary, 20:13) and "Señor mío" (Thomas, 20:28). Inside a plural_you span the two are not nested: the plural_you span is split around the deity_pronoun span, as in Mark 13:9.

decisions.choice: o Verbo (key term, the whole book, every level)
decisions.reason: "A Palavra" says "word, speech" more plainly and keeps the link to God speaking in Genesis 1 (meaning decision m2), but it is feminine: verse 2 would read "Ela estava no princípio junto de Deus", and the Word would be "ela" until becoming a man in verse 14. "O Verbo" is masculine, is the traditional Portuguese term (from the Latin Verbum) and keeps the pronouns natural; its weakness is that "verbo" today is mostly a grammar word, so the glossary explains that it means "the Word". As the Spanish "el Verbo" and the French "le Verbe" record. For review by a native speaker.

"Junto de" says presence beside a person, closer to the relational sense meaning decision m3 describes than the bare "com"; "voltado para" copies the preposition's basic sense, which the note keeps. Portuguese "estar" says where the Word was and "ser" ("era o Verbo", "era Deus") what he is; the imperfect carries the continuing sense, so only Readable adds "já" (already), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: ቃል (the Word), with no definite suffix, at every level and through the book
alternatives: ቃሉ (the word, with the definite suffix)
decisions.reason: "ቃል" is the ordinary Amharic word for a word, a saying and a promise, and the word the Ethiopian church has long used for the Logos. Without the definite suffix it reads as a name or title, as "the Word" does in English, so it is not mistaken for some word just mentioned. Readable keeps it rather than explaining it as "the message", because John goes on to say who the Word is (meaning decisions m2 and m4); the echo of God speaking in Genesis 1 (m1) stays audible.

decisions.choice: ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር (with God) ... አምላክ ነበረ (was God)
alternatives: ቃልም እግዚአብሔር ነበረ (the Word was እግዚአብሔር)
በእግዚአብሔር ዘንድ (with God, the older wording)
decisions.reason: Amharic has two words where English has one. "እግዚአብሔር" works as the name of the one God and here names the Father, the one the Word was with; "አምላክ" says what someone is: God, deity. The Greek has the article on the first "God" and none on the predicate (meaning decision m4: the Word is fully God, yet not the same person as the Father). "ቃልም እግዚአብሔር ነበረ" would make the Word the very person he was with; "አምላክ" says that the Word was truly God without saying that. "ጋር" is the plain modern word for being with a person, kept at every level.

decisions.choice: "वचन" (masculine) for the Word, at every level
decisions.reason: "वचन" is the word for something spoken, a word or a promise, so it keeps the link to God creating by speaking (meaning decision m2); "शब्द" is a single word or sound. As a noun it takes masculine singular agreement ("वचन था", "वचन देह बना"). Fixed for the whole of John.
As in the English Readable, the continuing "was" is made explicit, against "came into being" in verses 3, 6 and 14. "शुरू" is the everyday word beside Literal and Balanced "आरंभ".
The book-wide choice for John (docs/john-terms.md): 'Слово' is the living Russian word for the Word, and the capital shows that John means a person.

decisions.choice: 'и Богом было Слово' (L); 'и Слово было Богом' (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order, with 'Бог' first and without the article; the instrumental 'Богом' is the modern predicate form. Balanced and Readable use the ordinary Russian order.

The book-wide choice for John: "Слово" is the living Ukrainian word for the Word, and the capital shows that John means a person. Because "Слово" is neuter in Ukrainian, words that agree with it are neuter ("було", "воно") until 1:10, where the Greek itself turns to the person.

decisions.choice: "було в Бога" and "і Богом було Слово" (L); "з Богом" and "і Слово було Богом" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order with "Бог" first, in the instrumental that modern Ukrainian uses for a predicate, and renders *pros* by "в Бога" (at God's side). Balanced and Readable use the ordinary order and "з Богом" (with God).

decisions.choice: "言" (read ことば) for the Word, at every level and through the whole Gospel
decisions.reason: The single kanji 言 sets the Word apart from ordinary 言葉 (speech, words) and marks it as a name, while keeping the link to God creating by speaking (m2). "ロゴス" would bring in the Greek philosophy John does not develop. Readable keeps the same word because it is the Gospel's key term.

decisions.choice: light respect forms for what the Word (Jesus) and God do in the narration: "おられた", "来られた", "言われた" (L, B); "おられました", "言われました" (R)
alternatives: plain "あった", "来た" as for anyone else
decisions.reason: Japanese narration must choose a level of respect. As in all Japanese Open Word Bible narrative, the narrator uses the light 〜れる/〜られる forms for Jesus and God, and for no one else. The Word is a person here, so the prologue already says "おられた" rather than "あった". This holds for the whole Gospel.

decisions.choice: "Firman", capitalised, at every level and through the whole Gospel
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John (Terms, section 1). "Firman" is the Indonesian word for what God speaks, so it keeps the link to God creating by speaking (m2); the capital shows that John means a person. "Kalam" is the Islamic term for the speech of God and would pull the reader toward Qur'anic theology; "Sabda" is the Catholic word, and "Logos" brings in the Greek philosophy John does not develop.

decisions.choice: "Pada mulanya Firman sudah ada" (L, B); "Ketika segala sesuatu bermula, Firman sudah ada" (R)
decisions.reason: "Pada mulanya" is how Indonesian readers know the opening of Genesis 1:1, so it keeps the echo m1 asks for. "sudah ada" gives the continuing "was" of the imperfect, against "menjadi ada" (came into being) in verses 3 and 14.

decisions.reason: Verse 2 repeats verse 1 for emphasis. "He" reads naturally and the person is clear; Literal keeps "This one".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on Yeye or on the verb prefix
decisions.reason: Swahili marks the subject inside the verb (a-likuwa), and a prefix cannot take a capital. A free pronoun at the start of a sentence is capitalised anyway, as in English. So Swahili has fewer pronoun spans than English; the setting applies to free pronouns and possessives (yeye, wake, lake).

The Word is Jesus, and the narrator speaks of Jesus with honorific forms throughout (style guide section 4), so the pronouns that refer to the Word are honorific. The noun "वचन" itself keeps its grammatical singular agreement (1:1, 1:14).
'Слово' is neuter in Russian, so the pronoun that takes it up is 'оно'. The Greek 'this one' is masculine because the Greek noun is; Russian cannot keep both the gender and the reference.

The Greek pronoun agrees with *logos*, which is masculine; Ukrainian "Слово" is neuter, so the pronoun that agrees with it is "Воно". Readable repeats the noun to keep the sentence plain. The capital at the start of the sentence is ordinary, not a setting.

records.literal_gloss: All things through him came into being, and apart from him came into being not even one thing. What has come into being

en.B: All things came into being through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and without {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} nothing came into being that has come into being.
en.R: Everything was made through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Nothing that exists was made without {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Toutes choses vinrent à l’existence par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et en dehors de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pas une seule chose ne vint à l’existence de ce qui est venu à l’existence.

fr.R: Tout a commencé à exister par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Rien de ce qui existe n’a commencé à exister sans {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Vitu vyote vilikuja kuwako kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, na bila {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakikuja kuwako hata kitu kimoja kilichokuja kuwako.

decisions.choice: the clause ends verse 3: nothing came into being that has come into being
alternatives: the clause begins verse 4: what has come into being in him was life
decisions.reason: The manuscripts have no punctuation, so both readings are possible; the SBLGNT itself punctuates the other way, as did several early Christian writers. We follow the reading that most translations use because "what has come into being in him was life" is hard to make sense of. A footnote gives the other reading.
γίνομαι means to come to be, happen or become; it is not the usual word for create. The sense, creation through the Word, is the same either way.

decisions.choice: through him: the one through whom the Father acts
decisions.reason: διά with the genitive names the agent through whom someone acts. The Father creates through the Word.
Plain English for Readable; the meaning decision is unchanged.
"Por él" can mean "by him" as the maker. "Por medio de" keeps the Word as the one through whom the Father acts; the same phrase is used for Moses in verse 17.

decisions.choice: llegó a existir (L, B); se hizo (R)
decisions.reason: Follows the meaning decision; "se hizo" is the plain Spanish for Readable.

decisions.choice: passé simple for narrative past (L, B); passé composé (R); passé composé in speech and first-person testimony at every level
decisions.reason: The passé simple is the normal tense of written French narrative and suits a careful public reading. Readable uses the passé composé, the past tense of spoken French that young readers read and write today. Where people speak, or the writer speaks as a witness ("nous avons contemplé", 1:14), every level uses the passé composé as French does. Literal keeps the Greek present where John has it and the perfect as a passé composé ("ce qui est venu à l’existence").

decisions.choice: venir à l’existence par lui (L, B); commencer à exister par lui (R)
decisions.reason: With an intransitive verb, "par lui" reads as "through him", the one through whom the Father acts. A passive ("tout a été fait par lui") would make him the agent, "by him", and "créer" is not the Greek verb. Readable keeps the intransitive with plain words. In verse 17, where French needs a passive, "par l’intermédiaire de" is used for Moses.
"Kwa" can mean through, by, with or to, and "na" would make him the maker on his own. "Kupitia" (through) says he is the one through whom God made everything, as the meaning note has it.

"Kuja kuwako" (come to be) keeps the Greek verb's sense of coming into existence, distinct from "alikuwako" (was) in verse 1. Readable says "kiliumbwa" (was created), as the English Readable says "was made".

decisions.choice: "그분" with no deity_pronoun span, here and through the passage
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change and the Korean text carries no deity_pronoun spans. Respect for the Word is carried at every level by "그분" (that honoured person) and by the honorific -시- and 께서 on verbs and subjects.
"생겨나다" (come into being) keeps the Greek verb's sense of coming to exist, distinct from "계셨다" (was) in verse 1. Readable says "만들어졌다" (was made), as the English Readable says "was made".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} for the Word, Jesus and God in the narrative
decisions.reason: Vietnamese already has a respectful pronoun for God and for Jesus, "ngài"; the reader setting only decides whether it is capitalised in mid-sentence. At the start of a sentence it is written "Ngài" plainly. The Word is spoken of as "ngài" from here on, since the Word is a person.

decisions.choice: vir a existir por meio dele (L, B); ser feito por meio dele (R)
decisions.reason: "Por ele" after a passive names the maker ("by him"); "por meio de" keeps the Word as the one through whom the Father acts (meaning decision m3), and "vir a existir" keeps the Greek verb, which is not the usual word for create (m2). Readable says "foi feito", as the English Readable says "was made", but keeps "por meio dele". Verse 17 uses the same "por meio de" for Moses.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic: በእርሱ, ያለ እርሱ are written once
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the reader's setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change in Amharic. Pronouns for God and for Jesus are written plainly throughout John.

Devanagari has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Hindi. Respect for God and Jesus is carried by the honorific third person ("उनके", "उन्होंने") and by the forms of address, at every level.
The Greek verb means to come into being. 'Начало быть' is the familiar Synodal wording but is no longer ordinary Russian.
"Постати" (to come into being) keeps the one Greek verb repeated three times and does not narrow it to making; Readable says "створене", as the English Readable says "made".
"menjadi ada" keeps the one verb of coming into being (m2) without narrowing it to "created"; Readable says "dijadikan", as the English Readable says "made". "terjadi" would read as "happened".

decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπων here means humanity as a whole, so the gender setting applies.
The inclusive default says plainly what the word means; Traditional is one tap away.
Spanish "hombres" is often read as generic, but the inclusive default says it plainly.
French "homme" is read as generic less and less, so the inclusive default says plainly that all people are meant; the traditional "des hommes" is the alternative.

"Maisha" is a lifetime or the way one lives; "uzima" is life itself, the word Swahili uses for eternal life, so John's life-words stay one word. "Mwanga" is everyday light; "nuru" is light as a figure of God's presence and truth, which is what John means.

decisions.choice: no gender span: wanadamu (L), watu wote (B, R)
decisions.reason: The English offers "men" as a traditional alternative. Swahili "wanadamu" and "watu" already include men and women, and the only male alternative, "wanaume", means males and would change the meaning. So the Swahili has no gender span here or in verse 9.

decisions.choice: "사람들" / "모든 사람" with no gender span (here and in 1:9)
decisions.reason: The English offers "people" or "men" for a word meaning human beings. Korean "사람" already means a human being of either sex and has no generic masculine to offer as an alternative, so the gender setting has nothing to change here.

decisions.choice: "loài người" (L), "mọi người" (B, R) with no gender span
alternatives: a gender setting span as in the English
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người" already means a human being of either sex, so there is no second wording for the gender setting to offer; the English span has no Vietnamese counterpart here or in 1:9.

decisions.choice: ሕይወት (life) and ብርሃን (light), the same words at every level through John
alternatives: ብርሃን for light only at Literal
decisions.reason: Life and light are two of John's key words and return through the book (8:12; 11:25; 14:6). Amharic has one plain word for each, so it keeps them at every level as the English does; "ኑሮ" means a way or standard of living, not life itself.

decisions.choice: የሰዎች (of people) / ለሰዎች ሁሉ (for all people), with no gender span
alternatives: {{gender:ለሰዎች ሁሉ|ለሰው ልጆች ሁሉ}} as in the English
decisions.reason: "ሰዎች" (people) already includes men and women, and Amharic has no second wording that means "men" in the old generic sense, so the setting has nothing to switch. This holds for ሰው, ሰዎች and ማንም through the passage.

The English offers "people" or "men" as a setting. Hindi "मनुष्य" and "लोग" already mean human beings, women and men alike, so there is nothing for a gender setting to change. The same holds for "हर मनुष्य" in 1:9.

Light is one of John's threads (1:4-9; 3:19-21; 8:12; 12:35-46), so each level keeps one word for it through the book: "ज्योति" at Literal and Balanced, and the everyday "रोशनी" at Readable, as Matthew 5:14 Readable has it.
The English has a gender setting here. Russian 'люди' already means human beings of both sexes, so no setting is needed; the old 'человеков' only adds a Slavonic flavour, not a different sense.

The English has a gender span (people|men). Ukrainian "люди" already means human beings of both sexes, and the traditional Ukrainian wording is also "світло людей", so no alternative is needed. The same holds for "кожна людина" in 1:9.

decisions.choice: "人々" (L), "すべての人" (B, R) with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English needs a gender span because "men" is the traditional word; Japanese 人 and 人々 already mean people of either sex (m1), so there is nothing for the setting to switch. The same holds for "every person" in verse 9.

decisions.choice: "manusia" (L, B), "semua orang" (R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English has a gender span (people|men). Indonesian "manusia" and "orang" already mean human beings of either sex (m1), and no traditional Indonesian wording says "men" here, so the setting has nothing to switch. The same holds for "setiap orang" in verse 9.

decisions.reason: This word family runs through the whole Gospel and carries a courtroom sense. Keep it consistent where the level allows.
The pronoun refers to John: people believe through what he testifies.

"Croire par lui" is stiff in modern French. "Grâce à lui" says that people believe through John’s testimony, as the meaning decision reads it; because "lumière" is feminine, "lui" cannot be taken for the light.
As the English Readable, plain words for young readers; the courtroom sense of the word family stays at Literal and Balanced.

"증언" is the modern courtroom word for testimony, which the meaning decision asks for; "증거" now mostly means evidence. Readable says "알려 주다" (make known) as the English Readable says "tell people about".
The courtroom words of everyday Vietnamese, kept through the book for the testimony theme (with "lời chứng" for the noun). "Ông" is the narrator's pronoun for John the Baptist.

For the whole book (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 6): the key verb is "crer" / "crer em" at Literal and Balanced; Readable says the everyday "acreditar" where the English Readable says "believe", and "confiar" only where it says "trust". John never uses the noun "faith", so the verb is kept rather than "ter fé".

decisions.choice: ማመን (believe), the verb at every level; በ- for "believe in" (በእርሱ ማመን)
alternatives: እምነት እንዲኖራቸው (that they might have faith)
decisions.reason: John never uses the noun "faith"; he says "believe" ninety-eight times, and docs/john-terms.md keeps the verb at every level. Amharic "አመነ" covers both believing what someone says and believing in a person (with the prefix በ-), so one verb serves through the book. Its relative "ታመነ" (rely on) is kept for 2:24, where John plays on the two senses.

Testimony is a courtroom word in John (meaning decision m1), and it runs through the book; "ምስክርነት" and "መመስከር" are the Amharic words for a witness's evidence. Readable says "ሊነግራቸው" (to tell them), as the English Readable says "tell people".
Believe is a key term in John, who never uses the noun faith; Hindi keeps the verb "विश्वास करना" at every level, Readable included (docs/john-terms.md).
The courtroom word family (meaning decision m1) is kept as "गवाही देना" (testify) and "गवाह" (witness), the everyday legal words; Readable says what the witness did ("बताने आया").

decisions.choice: "証し", "証しする" at every level, through the Gospel; "証言" only for a witness in court (18:23)
decisions.reason: "証し" is the living Japanese word for this testimony and can carry the courtroom sense the whole Gospel gives it (m1); "証言" would sound only legal. Readable keeps the same word, which is plain enough, so the Gospel's thread of witnesses (1:7; 3:11; 5:31-39; 8:13-18; 15:26-27; 19:35; 21:24) stays visible.

The witness words keep their courtroom sense through the Gospel (m1); "kesaksian" and "bersaksi" are the ordinary Indonesian terms for testimony in court. Lowercase "dia" here is John, not Jesus, so it takes no span.

id.L: Terang yang sejati, yang menerangi setiap orang, sedang datang ke dalam dunia.

decisions.choice: the light was coming into the world
alternatives: every person who comes into the world
decisions.reason: The participle could agree with the light or with every person. John elsewhere speaks of the light coming into the world (3:19; 12:46), and verses 10-11 describe its arrival. A footnote gives the other reading.
Generic, so the gender setting applies.
"Enlightens" now suggests sudden understanding or the Enlightenment; "gives light to" keeps the image.
Inclusive default; Traditional one tap away.
As in verse 4.
French "éclairer" is both the literal sense and the plain word, so every level uses it, Literal included; "illuminer" leans toward sudden insight, the problem the English "enlightens" has.
As in verse 4. Readable says "tous les humains" to avoid "tout le monde ... dans le monde", where "monde" would carry two senses.

decisions.choice: inayomwangazia: the light keeps its own agreement
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable say "who gives light". In Swahili the verb must agree with "nuru" (i-), and a personal "anaye-" with "nuru" would read as an error. The person comes into view in verse 10, where the verbs turn personal (alikuwa, haukumtambua).
The style guide keeps "진리" for the noun truth and uses "참" for the adjective "true", so "참 빛" (the real, genuine light) is not confused with "light of truth".

decisions.choice: "thế gian" for the world (kosmos), every level
decisions.reason: "Thế gian" is the world of people as well as the created order, the range John's word covers; "thế giới" is the physical or political world and is kept for places where only that is meant. "thật" is the adjective for true ("ánh sáng thật").

The English Balanced avoids "enlightens"; Portuguese "iluminar" has no such association and keeps the image, while "dar luz a" would be heard as "dar à luz" (give birth). Readable says "traz luz para".

decisions.choice: ዓለም (the world), at every level through John
alternatives: የሰው ልጆች (humankind) where the sense is people
decisions.reason: "The world" is a key term in John, and a meaning decision says each time which sense it has: the created order, humanity, or humanity set against God. Amharic "ዓለም" carries all three, as the Greek word does, so it stays the same word at every level and the meaning decisions do the explaining; "ምድር" would narrow it to the earth.

decisions.choice: "संसार" for the world, at every level
decisions.reason: World is a key term in John, kept as "संसार" at every level, Readable included, so that the thread of the word stays visible through the book. Which sense the world has is a meaning decision.
The participle "coming" belongs with the light (meaning decision m1); the feminine "आनेवाली" agrees with "ज्योति", so Hindi cannot read it as "every man coming into the world".
'Просвещать' now chiefly means to educate. Balanced and Readable keep the picture of light falling on every person.
Russian 'человек' is a human being of either sex, so the English gender setting has no Russian counterpart here.
The adjective *alēthinos* (real, genuine) is not the key term "truth"; Readable uses the everyday word.
As in verse 4: "orang" already means any person, so the English gender span (everyone|every man) has no Indonesian counterpart. "sejati" is used for "true" in the sense of real (Style, section 7).

decisions.reason: John often uses καὶ where the sense is a contrast. Languages that need an explicit contrast should add one.
See the meaning decision.
English needs "though" to carry the irony.
From here John speaks of the Word as the person who came into the world, and of the light ('свет', masculine) of verse 9. Russian moves to the masculine, as Russian translations traditionally do.

The light ("світло") and the Word ("Слово") are neuter in Ukrainian, but here the Greek pronoun is masculine although *phōs* is neuter: John now speaks of the person. Ukrainian follows with the masculine. Forms such as "нього", "ньому" and "його" are the same for both genders.

vi.L: Ngài đã đến [nơi] của riêng mình, và những người của riêng mình đã không tiếp nhận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Ngài đến nơi thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và chính dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã không tiếp nhận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Ngài đến với dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhưng họ không chịu đón nhận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

pt.L: Para o que era {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} veio, e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} não {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} receberam.
pt.B: Ele veio para o que era {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}}, e o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} próprio povo não {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} recebeu.
pt.R: Ele veio para o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} próprio povo, mas eles não quiseram aceitá-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}.

am.L: ወደ ራሱ ወደ ሆነው መጣ፤ የራሱ የሆኑትም አልተቀበሉትም።
am.B: ወደ ራሱ ስፍራ መጣ፤ የራሱ ሕዝብ ግን አልተቀበለውም።
am.R: ወደ ገዛ ሕዝቡ መጣ፤ እነርሱ ግን ሊቀበሉት አልፈለጉም።

hi.L: वे अपने [घर] में आए, और उनके अपने [लोगों] ने उन्हें ग्रहण नहीं किया।
hi.B: वे उसमें आए जो उनका अपना था, और उनके अपने लोगों ने उन्हें ग्रहण नहीं किया।
hi.R: वे अपने ही लोगों के पास आए, पर उन्होंने उन्हें स्वीकार नहीं किया।

ru.L: В своё {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} пришёл, и свои {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} не приняли.
ru.B: Он пришёл в то, что принадлежало {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}}, и {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} собственный народ {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} не принял.
ru.R: Он пришёл к своему народу, но они не захотели {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} принять.

uk.L: До свого прийшов, і свої {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} не прийняли.
uk.B: Він прийшов до свого, і {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} власний народ не прийняв {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}.
uk.R: Він прийшов до свого народу, але люди не захотіли {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} прийняти.

ja.L: この方はご自分の[ところ]に来られた。そしてご自分の[民]はこの方を受け入れなかった。
ja.B: この方はご自分のところに来られたが、ご自分の民はこの方を受け入れなかった。
ja.R: この方は、ご自分の民のところに来られました。けれども、その人たちはこの方を受け入れようとしませんでした。

id.L: Dia datang kepada milik-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} sendiri, dan orang-orang milik-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} sendiri tidak menerima {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}.
id.B: Dia datang kepada apa yang menjadi milik-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, tetapi umat-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} sendiri tidak menerima {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}.
id.R: Dia datang kepada bangsa-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} sendiri, tetapi mereka tidak mau menerima {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}.

decisions.choice: his own place; his own people (Israel)
decisions.reason: The first is neuter (his own things, his own place); the second is masculine (his own people). Literal shows the difference; Readable may merge them.

French can keep the Greek distinction: "chez lui" is his own place (the neuter), "les siens" his own people (the masculine). Readable merges them as the meaning decision allows. "Les siens" takes no capital under the deity_pronoun setting: it names the people, not him.

decisions.choice: vilivyo vyake ... walio wake (L); kilicho chake ... watu wake (B)
decisions.reason: Swahili can use a possessive on its own, but "alikuja kwa vyake" is unclear. The class prefixes keep the Greek's two words apart: "vi-" for ἴδια (his own things, his own place) and "wa-" for ἴδιοι (his own people). Literal brackets the supporting "vilivyo", "walio".

Greek says "his own (things)" and "his own (people)" with no noun; Korean needs one, so Literal supplies the most neutral nouns in brackets. Balanced names the place and the people the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: "của riêng mình" (his own) with the reflexive "mình"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese uses the reflexive "mình" for "his own" after its subject; it is not a pronoun of respect, so it takes no setting span.

decisions.choice: o que era seu ... os seus
decisions.reason: Portuguese shows the neuter and the masculine of meaning decision m1 without brackets: "o que era seu" is his own place or things, and "os seus" is the ordinary way to say his own people.
The Greek has a neuter 'his own things' (his own place) and then a masculine 'his own people'. Literal keeps the two forms apart.
Where the English has "his own" under the setting, Ukrainian uses the reflexive "свій", which the style guide leaves without a span; "його" keeps the span where it is used.

source.text: ὅσοι δὲ ἔλαβον αὐτόν, ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τέκνα θεοῦ γενέσθαι, τοῖς πιστεύουσιν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, οἳ οὐκ ἐξ αἱμάτων οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος σαρκὸς οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος ἀνδρὸς ἀλλ’ ἐκ θεοῦ ἐγεννήθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: But as many as received him, he gave to them authority children of God to become, to the ones believing in his name, \v 13 who not from bloods nor from will of flesh nor from will of a husband but from God were born.

en.L: But as many as received {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them authority to become children of God, to those believing in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, \v 13 who were born not of bloods, nor of [the] will of [the] flesh, nor of [the] will of a husband, but of God.
en.B: But to all who received {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, who believed in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the right to become children of God— \v 13 children born not of blood, nor of human desire, nor of a husband's will, but born of God.
en.R: But some did accept {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. To them {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the right to become God's children. \v 13 They became {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children not by natural birth, not by human choice, not by a husband's decision, but because God gave them new birth.

es.L: Pero a cuantos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} recibieron, les dio autoridad de llegar a ser hijos de Dios, a los que creen en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre, \v 13 los cuales no nacieron de sangres, ni de voluntad de carne, ni de voluntad de varón, sino de Dios.
es.B: Pero a todos los que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} recibieron, a los que creen en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre, les dio el derecho de llegar a ser hijos de Dios. \v 13 Estos no nacieron de sangre, ni por deseo humano, ni por voluntad de un esposo, sino que nacieron de Dios.
es.R: Pero a los que sí {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aceptaron y creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, les dio el derecho de ser hijos de Dios. \v 13 Llegaron a ser {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hijos no por nacimiento natural, ni por decisión humana, ni por decisión de un esposo, sino porque Dios los hizo nacer.

fr.L: Mais à tous ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} reçurent, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donna l’autorité de devenir enfants de Dieu, à ceux qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom, \v 13 qui naquirent non des sangs, ni de [la] volonté de [la] chair, ni de [la] volonté d’un mari, mais de Dieu.
fr.B: Mais à tous ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accueillirent, à ceux qui croient en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} nom, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donna le droit de devenir enfants de Dieu, \v 13 des enfants qui ne sont nés ni du sang, ni d’un désir humain, ni de la volonté d’un mari, mais qui sont nés de Dieu.
fr.R: Mais certains {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont accueilli et ont cru en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. À ceux-là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a donné le droit de devenir enfants de Dieu. \v 13 Ils sont devenus {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} enfants, non par une naissance naturelle, ni par une décision humaine, ni par la décision d’un mari, mais parce que c’est Dieu qui les a fait naître.

sw.L: Lakini wote waliompokea, aliwapa mamlaka ya kuwa watoto wa Mungu, wale wanaoamini katika jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, \v 13 ambao hawakuzaliwa kutokana na damu, wala kutokana na mapenzi ya mwili, wala kutokana na mapenzi ya mume, bali kutokana na Mungu.
sw.B: Lakini wote waliompokea, wale wanaoliamini jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, aliwapa mamlaka ya kuwa watoto wa Mungu. \v 13 Hawa hawakuzaliwa kwa damu, wala kwa tamaa ya kibinadamu, wala kwa mapenzi ya mume, bali walizaliwa na Mungu.
sw.R: Lakini wengine walimpokea na kumwamini. Hao aliwapa uwezo wa kuwa watoto wa Mungu. \v 13 Hawakuwa watoto {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa kuzaliwa kimwili, wala kwa uamuzi wa binadamu, wala kwa uamuzi wa mume, bali kwa sababu Mungu ndiye aliyewazaa.

ko.L: 그러나 그분을 받아들인 사람들 모두에게, 그분은 하나님의 자녀가 될 권한을 주셨다. 곧 그분의 이름을 믿는 사람들에게 [주셨다]. \v 13 그들은 피들에서도, 육의 뜻에서도, 남편의 뜻에서도 나지 않고, 하나님께로부터 났다.
ko.B: 그러나 그분을 받아들인 사람들, 곧 그분의 이름을 믿는 사람들에게는 하나님의 자녀가 될 권리를 주셨다. \v 13 이 자녀들은 혈통이나 사람의 욕망이나 남편의 뜻으로 태어난 것이 아니라, 하나님께로부터 태어났다.
ko.R: 그러나 그분을 받아들이고 믿은 사람들도 있었다. 그분은 그들에게 하나님의 자녀가 될 권리를 주셨다. \v 13 그들이 하나님의 자녀가 된 것은 사람의 몸으로 태어났기 때문도, 사람이 원해서도, 남편이 결정해서도 아니었다. 하나님께서 그들을 새로 태어나게 하셨기 때문이다.

vi.L: Nhưng hễ ai đã tiếp nhận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban cho họ quyền trở nên con cái Đức Chúa Trời, [tức là] cho những người tin vào danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \v 13 là những người đã được sinh ra không phải bởi các dòng máu, cũng không phải bởi ý muốn của xác thịt, cũng không phải bởi ý muốn của người chồng, nhưng bởi Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Nhưng hễ ai tiếp nhận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, tức là những người tin vào danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ban cho quyền trở nên con cái Đức Chúa Trời— \v 13 là những người con được sinh ra không bởi huyết thống, không bởi ham muốn của con người, cũng không bởi ý muốn của người chồng, nhưng được sinh ra bởi Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Nhưng cũng có những người tiếp nhận {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và tin vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài ban cho họ quyền trở nên con cái Đức Chúa Trời. \v 13 Họ trở thành con cái của Đức Chúa Trời không phải do sinh ra theo lẽ tự nhiên, không phải do con người quyết định, cũng không phải do ý người chồng, mà vì chính Đức Chúa Trời đã cho họ được sinh ra.

pt.L: Mas a todos quantos {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} receberam, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} deu autoridade de se tornarem filhos de Deus, aos que creem no {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} nome, \v 13 os quais nasceram não de sangues, nem da vontade da carne, nem da vontade de [um] marido, mas de Deus.
pt.B: Mas a todos os que {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} receberam, aos que creem no {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} nome, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} deu o direito de se tornarem filhos de Deus, \v 13 filhos que não nasceram do sangue, nem do desejo humano, nem da vontade de um marido, mas nasceram de Deus.
pt.R: Mas algumas pessoas {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} aceitaram e acreditaram {{deity_pronoun:nele|Nele}}. A elas {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} deu o direito de se tornarem filhos de Deus. \v 13 Elas se tornaram filhos {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, não por nascimento natural, nem por escolha humana, nem pela decisão de um marido, mas porque Deus lhes deu um novo nascimento.

am.L: ነገር ግን ለተቀበሉት ሁሉ የእግዚአብሔር ልጆች ይሆኑ ዘንድ ሥልጣንን ሰጣቸው፤ [ይህም] በስሙ ለሚያምኑት ነው፤ \v 13 እነርሱም ከደም ወይም ከሥጋ ፈቃድ ወይም ከባል ፈቃድ ሳይሆን ከእግዚአብሔር የተወለዱ ናቸው።
am.B: ነገር ግን ለተቀበሉት፣ በስሙም ላመኑት ሁሉ የእግዚአብሔር ልጆች የመሆን መብት ሰጣቸው፤ \v 13 እነዚህ ልጆች የተወለዱት ከደም ወይም ከሰው ምኞት ወይም ከባል ፈቃድ አይደለም፤ ከእግዚአብሔር ነው እንጂ።
am.R: ነገር ግን አንዳንዶች ተቀበሉት፤ በእርሱም አመኑ። ለእነርሱም የእግዚአብሔር ልጆች የመሆን መብት ሰጣቸው። \v 13 የእርሱ ልጆች የሆኑት በተፈጥሮ ልደት፣ በሰው ምርጫ ወይም በባል ውሳኔ አይደለም፤ እግዚአብሔር አዲስ ልደት ስለ ሰጣቸው ነው እንጂ።

hi.L: पर जितनों ने उन्हें ग्रहण किया, उन्होंने उन्हें परमेश्वर की सन्तान बनने का अधिकार दिया, अर्थात् उन्हें जो उनके नाम पर विश्वास करते हैं, \v 13 जो न लहुओं से, न शरीर की इच्छा से, न पति की इच्छा से, परंतु परमेश्वर से जन्मे।
hi.B: पर जितनों ने उन्हें ग्रहण किया, अर्थात् जिन्होंने उनके नाम पर विश्वास किया, उन सबको उन्होंने परमेश्वर की सन्तान बनने का अधिकार दिया। \v 13 ये वे सन्तान हैं जो न लहू से, न मनुष्य की इच्छा से, न पति की इच्छा से, परंतु परमेश्वर से जन्मी हैं।
hi.R: पर कुछ लोगों ने उन्हें स्वीकार किया और उन पर विश्वास किया। उन्हें उन्होंने परमेश्वर की सन्तान बनने का अधिकार दिया। \v 13 वे परमेश्वर की सन्तान इसलिए नहीं बने कि वे किसी ख़ानदान में पैदा हुए, या किसी मनुष्य ने ऐसा चाहा, या किसी पति ने ऐसा फ़ैसला किया। वे इसलिए उनकी सन्तान बने कि परमेश्वर ने ख़ुद उन्हें नया जन्म दिया।

ru.L: А всем, которые приняли {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} дал власть стать детьми Божьими, верящим в {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} имя, \v 13 которые не от кровей, и не от воли плоти, и не от воли мужа, но от Бога родились.
ru.B: А всем, кто принял {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} и поверил в {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} имя, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} дал право стать детьми Божьими — \v 13 детьми, рождёнными не от крови, не от человеческого желания и не от воли мужа, а от Бога.
ru.R: Но некоторые приняли {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} и поверили в {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}}. Им {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} дал право стать Божьими детьми. \v 13 Они стали {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} детьми не через обычное рождение, не по человеческому выбору и не по решению мужа, а потому, что Бог дал им новое рождение.

uk.L: А скільки [їх] прийняли {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, дав їм владу стати дітьми Божими, тим, що вірять у {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} імʼя, \v 13 які не з кровей, ані з волі тіла, ані з волі чоловіка, а від Бога народилися.
uk.B: А всім, хто прийняв {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, хто повірив у {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} імʼя, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} дав право стати Божими дітьми — \v 13 дітьми, народженими не від крові, не з людського бажання і не з волі чоловіка, а від Бога.
uk.R: Але деякі все ж прийняли {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} і повірили в {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}. Їм {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} дав право стати Божими дітьми. \v 13 Вони стали {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} дітьми не через звичайне народження, не з людського вибору і не з рішення чоловіка, а тому, що Бог дав їм нове народження.

ja.L: しかし、この方を受け入れた者たちには皆、神の子どもとなる権威をお与えになった。[すなわち]その名を信じる者たちに。\v 13 この者たちは、血からでも、肉の意志からでも、夫の意志からでもなく、神から生まれたのである。
ja.B: しかし、この方を受け入れた人々、すなわちその名を信じる人々には、神の子どもとなる権利をお与えになった。\v 13 この人々は、血筋によってでも、人の欲求によってでも、夫の意志によってでもなく、神によって生まれたのである。
ja.R: けれども、この方を受け入れて信じた人たちもいました。この方は、その人たちに神の子どもになる権利を与えてくださいました。\v 13 その人たちが神の子どもになったのは、生まれた家の血筋のためでも、人が望んだからでも、夫が決めたからでもありません。神が新しく生まれさせてくださったからです。

id.L: Tetapi sebanyak orang yang menerima {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}, {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} memberi mereka hak untuk menjadi anak-anak Allah, [yaitu] kepada mereka yang percaya kepada nama-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, \v 13 yang lahir bukan dari darah, dan bukan dari keinginan daging, dan bukan dari keinginan seorang suami, melainkan dari Allah.
id.B: Tetapi semua orang yang menerima {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}, yang percaya kepada nama-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, diberi-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} hak untuk menjadi anak-anak Allah, \v 13 anak-anak yang lahir bukan dari keturunan, bukan dari keinginan manusia, dan bukan dari kehendak seorang suami, melainkan lahir dari Allah.
id.R: Tetapi ada orang-orang yang mau menerima {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} dan percaya kepada-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}. Kepada mereka {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} memberi hak untuk menjadi anak-anak Allah. \v 13 Mereka menjadi anak-anak-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}} bukan karena kelahiran biasa, bukan karena keinginan manusia, dan bukan karena keputusan seorang suami, tetapi karena Allah sendiri memberi mereka hidup baru.

decisions.reason: The word means a right given, not an ability.

decisions.choice: children of God, of either sex
decisions.reason: τέκνα is neuter and already inclusive, so the gender setting does not apply.
In Hebrew thought a name stands for the person.
Spanish "hijos" is the ordinary word for children of both sexes. Adding "e hijas" would add words the Greek does not have.
The plural is an idiom for physical descent. Being born a Jew does not make someone God's child.
σάρξ here means ordinary human nature, not sinful nature as in Paul.
ἀνήρ is male; in a sentence about conception it means the husband. The gender setting does not apply.

alternatives: singular "who was born", referring to Christ
decisions.reason: The singular has only weak, mainly Latin, support. We follow the Greek manuscripts; a footnote names the variant because it changes who is meant.
Spanish has a word for male, "varón", which Literal uses to keep the distinction. Balanced and Readable follow the meaning decision.
French "le pouvoir de" usually means the ability to do something; the meaning decision says a right is granted, not an ability.
French has no ordinary word for "male" that Literal could use like the Spanish "varón", and "un homme" would be read as "a human being". "Un mari" says what the meaning decision says at every level.

"Haki" is the usual word for a right, but it is the settled word for righteousness, so it is kept for that. "Mamlaka" (authority) says a granted right; Readable says "uwezo" (the power, the means) as simpler Swahili.

The English Readable says "God gave them new birth". "Ndiye aliyewazaa" (it is God who gave them birth) is the plain Swahili for the same thing and keeps the contrast with the three ways they were not born.
The meaning decision reads a granted right or authority. "권한" keeps the sense of authority given by someone; "권리" (right) is the plainer modern word. "권세" sounds like political power.
Literal keeps the Greek plural "bloods" with "피들", which is unusual in Korean but grammatical and shows the reader what the Greek says; Balanced gives the sense, physical descent.

decisions.choice: "tin"; "tin vào" for the construction with eis (key term)
decisions.reason: John always uses the verb, so Vietnamese keeps the verb "tin" at every level, Readable included; "tin vào" renders believing into someone. "danh" is the word for a name when it stands for the person, as here.
"con cái" means children of either sex, so no gender setting is needed.

Meaning decision m1: the word is a right or authority that is granted. Literal keeps "ሥልጣን", the usual word for granted authority; Balanced and Readable say "መብት" (right), which fits becoming someone's children better in Amharic. "ኃይል" would make it strength, which the Greek does not say.
Literal keeps the Greek plural "bloods", an idiom for physical descent (meaning decision m4); Balanced says "लहू" and Readable "किसी ख़ानदान में पैदा हुए" (born into some family).
The Greek word is authority granted to someone. Literal keeps 'власть'; Balanced and Readable say 'право', which is what the granted authority amounts to here.
'Чада' and the form 'Божии' are Church Slavonic. 'Дети' covers sons and daughters, so no gender setting is needed.
*Exousia* is a granted right or authority (meaning decision). Literal keeps the older "влада"; Balanced and Readable say "право", which modern readers hear as a right given to them, not as power.

decisions.choice: "神の子ども" for the children of God
decisions.reason: "神の子" is the Japanese for the title Son of God, which John keeps for Jesus. "子ども" keeps believers, sons and daughters alike (m2), distinct from him.
m1: the word means a right granted, not a power or ability, so "hak" rather than "kuasa".

source.text: Καὶ ὁ λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ ἐθεασάμεθα τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, δόξαν ὡς μονογενοῦς παρὰ πατρός, πλήρης χάριτος καὶ ἀληθείας·

records.literal_gloss: And the word flesh became and pitched his tent among us, and we beheld his glory, glory as of an only one from a father, full of grace and truth.

en.L: And the Word became flesh and tabernacled among us, and we beheld {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, glory as of [the] one and only [Son] from [the] Father, full of grace and truth.
en.B: The Word became flesh and made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home among us. We have seen {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.
en.R: The Word became a human being and lived among us. We saw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, the glory of the Father's one and only Son, full of grace and truth.

es.L: Y el Verbo se hizo carne y acampó entre nosotros, y contemplamos {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria, gloria como del unigénito del Padre, lleno de gracia y de verdad.
es.B: El Verbo se hizo carne e hizo {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} morada entre nosotros. Hemos visto {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria, la gloria del Hijo único que viene del Padre, lleno de gracia y de verdad.
es.R: El Verbo se hizo hombre y vivió entre nosotros. Vimos {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria, la gloria del Hijo único del Padre, lleno de gracia y de verdad.

fr.L: Et le Verbe devint chair et dressa {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tente parmi nous, et nous avons contemplé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire, gloire comme [celle] du [Fils] unique [venu] d’auprès du Père, plein de grâce et de vérité.
fr.B: Le Verbe devint chair et établit {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} demeure parmi nous. Nous avons contemplé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire, la gloire du Fils unique venu d’auprès du Père, plein de grâce et de vérité.
fr.R: Le Verbe est devenu un être humain et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a vécu parmi nous. Nous avons vu {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire, la gloire du Fils unique du Père, plein de grâce et de vérité.

sw.L: Na Neno akawa mwili, akapiga hema kati yetu, na tukautazama utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, utukufu kama wa [Mwana] wa pekee kutoka kwa Baba, amejaa neema na kweli.
sw.B: Neno akawa mwili, akafanya makao {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kati yetu. Tumeuona utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, utukufu wa Mwana wa pekee aliyetoka kwa Baba, akiwa amejaa neema na kweli.
sw.R: Neno akawa binadamu, akaishi pamoja nasi. Tuliuona utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, utukufu wa Mwana wa pekee wa Baba, aliyejaa neema na kweli.

ko.L: 그리고 말씀이 육신이 되셔서 우리 가운데 장막을 치셨고, 우리는 그분의 영광을 보았는데, 아버지께로부터 [온] 유일한 [아들]의 영광 같은 영광이었으며, [그분은] 은혜와 진리로 가득하셨다.
ko.B: 말씀이 육신이 되셔서 우리 가운데 거처를 정하셨다. 우리는 그분의 영광을 보았다. 그것은 아버지께로부터 오신 유일한 아들의 영광이었고, 그분은 은혜와 진리로 가득하셨다.
ko.R: 말씀이 사람이 되셔서 우리와 함께 사셨다. 우리는 그분의 영광을 보았다. 그것은 아버지의 하나뿐인 아들의 영광이었다. 그분은 은혜와 진리로 가득하셨다.

vi.L: Và Ngôi Lời đã trở nên xác thịt và đã dựng lều giữa chúng tôi, và chúng tôi đã chiêm ngưỡng vinh quang {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vinh quang như của [Con] độc nhất từ nơi Cha, đầy ân điển và chân lý.
vi.B: Ngôi Lời đã trở nên xác thịt và cư ngụ giữa chúng tôi. Chúng tôi đã thấy vinh quang {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vinh quang của Con độc nhất đến từ Cha, đầy ân điển và chân lý.
vi.R: Ngôi Lời đã trở thành một con người và sống giữa chúng tôi. Chúng tôi đã thấy vinh quang {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là vinh quang của Con duy nhất của Cha, đầy ân điển và chân lý.

pt.L: E o Verbo se tornou carne e armou [a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}}] tenda entre nós, e contemplamos a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} glória, glória como do único [Filho] da parte do Pai, cheio de graça e de verdade.
pt.B: O Verbo se tornou carne e fez a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} morada entre nós. Nós vimos a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} glória, a glória do Filho único que vem do Pai, cheio de graça e de verdade.
pt.R: O Verbo se tornou um ser humano e viveu entre nós. Nós vimos a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} glória, a glória do Filho único do Pai, cheio de graça e de verdade.

am.L: ቃልም ሥጋ ሆነ፤ በመካከላችንም ድንኳን ተከለ፤ ክብሩንም ተመለከትን፤ [ይህም] ከአብ ዘንድ የመጣ የአንድያ [ልጅ] ክብር የሚመስል ክብር [ነው]፤ [እርሱም] ጸጋንና እውነትን የተሞላ [ነበረ]።

ru.L: И Слово стало плотью и раскинуло шатёр среди нас, и мы созерцали {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} славу, славу как единственного [Сына] от Отца, полное благодати и истины.
ru.B: Слово стало плотью и поселилось среди нас, полное благодати и истины. Мы видели {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} славу, славу единственного Сына от Отца.

uk.L: І Слово тілом стало, і розбило намет серед нас, і ми споглядали {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} славу, славу як єдиного [Сина] від Отця, повне благодаті та істини.
uk.B: Слово стало тілом і оселилося серед нас. Ми бачили {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} славу — славу єдиного Сина від Отця, сповненого благодаті та істини.

ja.L: そして言は肉となって、わたしたちの間に幕屋を張られた。そしてわたしたちはその栄光を見つめた。父からの、ただひとりの[子]としての栄光であって、[この方は]恵みと真理に満ちておられた。
ja.B: 言は肉となって、わたしたちの間に住まわれた。わたしたちは、その栄光をこの目で見た。それは父から来られたひとり子の栄光であり、この方は恵みと真理に満ちておられた。
ja.R: 言は人となって、わたしたちといっしょに暮らされました。わたしたちは、その栄光を自分の目で見ました。それは、父のひとり子の栄光でした。この方は、恵みと真理に満ちておられました。

id.L: Dan Firman itu menjadi daging dan berkemah di antara kami, dan kami telah memandang kemuliaan-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, kemuliaan seperti [kemuliaan] Anak yang tunggal dari Bapa, penuh kasih karunia dan kebenaran.
id.B: Firman itu menjadi daging dan tinggal di antara kami. Kami telah melihat kemuliaan-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, kemuliaan Anak yang tunggal, yang datang dari Bapa, penuh kasih karunia dan kebenaran.
id.R: Firman itu menjadi manusia dan hidup di antara kami. Kami melihat kemuliaan-{{deity_pronoun:nya|Nya}}, kemuliaan Anak satu-satunya dari Bapa. Dia penuh kasih karunia dan kebenaran.

alternatives: took on the appearance of a body
decisions.reason: The phrase is deliberately blunt: the eternal Word became fully human. Literal and Balanced keep the original image; Readable may say what it means.

decisions.choice: lived among us as God's glory lived in the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The verb means to live in a tent and recalls the tabernacle, where God's glory dwelt among Israel (Exodus 25:8; 40:34). The next words, about seeing his glory, complete the picture.
We looked at him ourselves (compare 1 John 1:1).
μονογενής is built from μόνος (only) and γένος (kind), not from γεννάω (beget); Hebrews 11:17 uses it of Isaac, who was not Abraham's only son. "Only begotten" came through the Latin unigenitus.

decisions.choice: full of grace and truth (key term: grace)
alternatives: full of unfailing love and faithfulness
decisions.reason: Probably echoes God's self-description in Exodus 34:6, abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness (Hebrew hesed and emet). "Grace" stays a key term; the note gives the Exodus link.
Greek leaves the noun unstated, but "from the Father" and John 3:16, 18 make "Son" clear.
"Acampó" keeps the tent image for Literal; "morada" recalls the dwelling of God's glory.
Jesus is a specific man, so the gender rule does not apply; "se hizo hombre" is also the phrase of the Nicene Creed in Spanish.
In today's Spanish "unigénito" just means an only child, so Literal may use it. Balanced and Readable avoid it because "-génito" suggests "begotten", the reading the meaning decision rejects.

decisions.choice: dressa sa tente (L); établit sa demeure (B); a vécu (R)
decisions.reason: "Dresser sa tente" keeps the tent image of the verb for Literal; "demeure" recalls the dwelling of God’s glory in the tabernacle, which the footnote explains. Readable says plainly what it means.

decisions.choice: le Fils unique, with "[Fils]" bracketed at Literal
decisions.reason: "Engendré" says "begotten", the reading the meaning decision rejects, and "monogène" is not French. "Unique" alone cannot stand as a noun in a natural sentence here, so Literal also supplies "Fils" in brackets, as the English Literal supplies "Son". "D’auprès du Père" (L, B) echoes "auprès de Dieu" in verse 1.

The narration is in the passé simple, but here the writer speaks as an eyewitness in the first person, and French uses the passé composé for that; "nous contemplâmes" would sound archaic even at Literal.

decisions.choice: akapiga hema (L); akafanya makao yake (B); akaishi (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of pitching a tent, which points to the tabernacle; Balanced says he made his dwelling among us; Readable says simply that he lived with us.
"Akawa mwili" (became flesh) can read in Swahili as "became a body". Readable says "binadamu" (a human being), as the English Readable says "a human being".

"Neema" is grace at every level. For truth, "kweli" is the older noun and still standard, and it is also the adjective "true" in verse 9 (nuru ya kweli), keeping John's link between them. "Ukweli" is the everyday modern noun; a native reviewer may prefer it, at least at Readable.

The meaning decision reads the word as unique, one of a kind, not as "only-begotten". "독생자" (only-begotten son), the familiar older word, stresses begetting; "유일한" and "하나뿐인" say unique in current Korean.

Literal keeps the tent picture so the tabernacle allusion stays visible; Balanced says he took up his dwelling; Readable says plainly that he lived with us. "은혜" and "진리" are key terms and stay the same at every level.

decisions.choice: key terms: "ân điển" (grace), "chân lý" (truth), "vinh quang" (glory), the same at every level
decisions.reason: Key terms keep one Vietnamese word through the book so readers can follow them. "sự thật" is kept for a plain fact; "chân lý" is truth as God's reality.

decisions.choice: exclusive "chúng tôi" (we, not including the reader) for the eyewitnesses
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must choose between "we" with or without the hearer. The meaning decision reads "we beheld" as an eyewitness claim, so "chúng tôi"; "among us" follows it. In 1:16 "we all received" includes every believer and is "chúng ta".

decisions.choice: "dựng lều" (pitched a tent) at L; "cư ngụ" (B), "sống" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the tent that the allusion to the tabernacle rests on.

decisions.choice: o único [Filho] (L); o Filho único (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Unigênito", familiar from older Portuguese Bibles, means "only begotten", the sense meaning decision m4 sets aside (it came through the Latin unigenitus). "Filho único" says unique, one of a kind, in everyday words.
Portuguese has no verb for "tabernacled", so Literal keeps the image of meaning decision m2 with "armou tenda"; Balanced says "fez a sua morada", Readable "viveu".

decisions.choice: ጸጋ (grace), እውነት (truth), ክብር (glory): one word each, at every level through John
decisions.reason: Grace, truth and glory are key terms (data/key_terms.json), kept as the same word at every level. "ጸጋ" is God's free gift and favour, where "ቸርነት" is a person's kindness; "ክብር" is both glory and honour, as the Greek word is, and links to "glorify" (ማክበር) later in John, where "ግርማ" is only splendour; "እውነት" is truth as faithfulness and reality, not a mere fact.

decisions.choice: ድንኳን ተከለ (pitched a tent, L); መኖሪያውን አደረገ (made his home, B); ኖረ (lived, R); አንድያ (one and only)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the tabernacle (meaning decision m2) with the plain words for pitching a tent; Balanced and Readable say where he lived. "አንድያ" means an only child, one of a kind, which is the sense of meaning decision m4; Literal brackets "ልጅ" (son), which the Greek leaves to be understood.
"डेरा डालना" is to pitch a tent or camp, so Hindi keeps the tabernacle image of meaning decision m2. Readable says plainly "हमारे बीच रहा" (lived among us).

Grace and truth are key terms (style guide section 6): "अनुग्रह" at every level, Readable included; truth is "सत्य" in Literal and Balanced and the everyday "सच" in Readable, through the whole of John.
Literal keeps the blunt "became flesh" (meaning decision m1); Balanced uses the established "देहधारी हुआ" (took a body); Readable says what it means, "एक इंसान बना".
The Greek verb means to pitch a tent; the meaning decision links it to God's glory dwelling in the tabernacle. Literal keeps the tent.
Russian must give 'full' a gender. It is made to agree with 'Слово', the subject of the sentence, as most readers take the Greek.
The style guide's key term for truth: 'истина' at Literal and Balanced, the everyday 'правда' at Readable.
The Greek verb means to pitch a tent and recalls the tabernacle (meaning decision); Literal keeps the picture, Balanced and Readable say what it means.

*Monogenēs* means unique, one of a kind (meaning decision). The church word "Єдинородний" suggests 'only-begotten'; "єдиний" says unique. In Literal the adjective "повне" agrees with "Слово", as the Greek *plērēs* most likely goes with the Word.

decisions.choice: "ひとり子" (B, R; also 1:18, 3:16, 3:18); "ただひとりの[子]" (L)
decisions.reason: μονογενής means unique, the only one of his kind (m4). "ひとり子" says the only child without the old "only begotten" overtone, and is written in kana as modern writing does. Literal keeps the Greek's missing noun visible in brackets.

Indonesian must choose between inclusive "kita" and exclusive "kami". The "we" of this verse are the eyewitnesses who saw his glory (m3), not every reader, so the brief's choice is "kami" (Style, section 5). Verse 16 turns to the whole believing community and says "kita".

decisions.choice: "Anak yang tunggal" (L, B, with "[kemuliaan]" supplied at L); "Anak satu-satunya" (R)
decisions.reason: m4: unique, one of a kind. Indonesian supplies "Anak", as the English supplies "Son", and "yang tunggal" keeps the adjective as an adjective. "berkemah" at Literal keeps the tabernacle picture of m2.

source.text: Ἰωάννης μαρτυρεῖ περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ κέκραγεν λέγων· Οὗτος ἦν ὃν εἶπον· Ὁ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος ἔμπροσθέν μου γέγονεν, ὅτι πρῶτός μου ἦν·

records.literal_gloss: John testifies about him and has cried out saying, "This was he whom I said: 'The one after me coming ahead of me has become, because first of me he was.'"

en.L: John testifies about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and has cried out, saying, "This was {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} of whom I said, 'The one coming after me has come to be ahead of me, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was before me.'"
en.B: John testified about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and cried out, "This is the one I meant when I said, 'He who comes after me ranks ahead of me, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} existed before me.'"
en.R: John told people about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He shouted, "This is the one I was talking about! I said, 'Someone is coming after me who is greater than I am, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} existed before me.'"

es.L: Juan da testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y ha clamado diciendo: «Este era aquel de quien dije: “El que viene después de mí ha llegado a estar delante de mí, porque era antes que yo”».
es.B: Juan dio testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y exclamó: «Este es aquel de quien yo dije: “El que viene después de mí es superior a mí, porque existía antes que yo”».
es.R: Juan habló de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a la gente. Gritó: «¡Este es de quien yo hablaba! Dije: “Viene alguien después de mí que es más importante que yo, porque existía antes que yo”».

fr.L: Jean rend témoignage de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et a crié en disant : « Celui-ci était celui dont j’ai dit : “Celui qui vient après moi est passé devant moi, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était avant moi.” »
fr.B: Jean rendit témoignage de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et s’écria : « C’est de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que je parlais quand j’ai dit : “Celui qui vient après moi est placé au-dessus de moi, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} existait avant moi.” »
fr.R: Jean a parlé de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} aux gens. Il a crié : « C’est de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que je parlais ! J’ai dit : “Quelqu’un vient après moi, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est plus grand que moi, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} existait avant moi.” »

sw.L: Yohana anashuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, naye amepaza sauti akisema, "Huyu alikuwa ndiye niliyesema habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}: 'Anayekuja nyuma yangu amekuwa mbele yangu, kwa sababu alikuwa kabla yangu.'"
sw.B: Yohana alishuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, akapaza sauti, "Huyu ndiye niliyesema habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}: 'Anayekuja baada yangu ni mkuu kuliko mimi, kwa sababu alikuwako kabla yangu.'"
sw.R: Yohana aliwaambia watu habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Alipaza sauti, "Huyu ndiye niliyekuwa nikimzungumzia! Nilisema, 'Anakuja mtu baada yangu aliye mkuu kuliko mimi, kwa sababu alikuwepo kabla yangu.'"

ko.L: 요한이 그분에 대하여 증언하고, 외치며 말한다. "이분이 내가 말한 그분이었다. '내 뒤에 오시는 분이 나보다 앞서게 되셨다. 그분이 나보다 먼저 계셨기 때문이다.'"
ko.B: 요한은 그분에 대하여 증언하며 외쳤다. "이분이 바로 내가 말한 분이다. '내 뒤에 오시는 분이 나보다 앞서신다. 그분은 나보다 먼저 계셨기 때문이다.'"
ko.R: 요한은 사람들에게 그분에 대해 알렸다. 그는 큰 소리로 외쳤다. "내가 말하던 분이 바로 이분이다! 나는 '내 뒤에 오시는 분은 나보다 더 크신 분이다. 그분은 나보다 먼저 계셨기 때문이다' 하고 말했다."

vi.L: Giăng làm chứng về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và đã kêu lên rằng: "Đây là Đấng mà tôi đã nói đến: 'Đấng đến sau tôi đã vượt lên trước tôi, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã có trước tôi.'"
vi.B: Giăng đã làm chứng về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và kêu lớn: "Đây là Đấng tôi muốn nói khi bảo rằng: 'Đấng đến sau tôi thì cao trọng hơn tôi, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hiện hữu trước tôi.'"
vi.R: Giăng nói cho mọi người biết về {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ông kêu lớn: "Đây là Đấng tôi đã nói đến! Tôi đã nói: 'Có một Đấng đến sau tôi nhưng lớn hơn tôi, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã có trước tôi.'"

pt.L: João testemunha a respeito {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} e tem clamado, dizendo: "Este era aquele de quem eu disse: 'Aquele que vem depois de mim passou à minha frente, porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} era antes de mim.'"
pt.B: João deu testemunho a respeito {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}} e proclamou em alta voz: "Este é aquele de quem eu falava quando disse: 'Aquele que vem depois de mim está acima de mim, porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} já existia antes de mim.'"
pt.R: João falou às pessoas sobre {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. Ele gritou: "É deste que eu estava falando! Eu disse: 'Vem depois de mim alguém que é maior do que eu, porque {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} já existia antes de mim.'"

am.L: ዮሐንስ ስለ እርሱ ይመሰክራል፤ እንዲህ እያለም ጮኋል፦ «እንዲህ ብዬ የተናገርኩለት ይህ ነበረ፦ “ከእኔ በኋላ የሚመጣው ከእኔ በፊት ሆኗል፤ ከእኔ አስቀድሞ ነበረና።”»
am.B: ዮሐንስ ስለ እርሱ መሰከረ፤ ድምፁንም ከፍ አድርጎ እንዲህ አለ፦ «“ከእኔ በኋላ የሚመጣው ከእኔ ይበልጣል፤ ከእኔ በፊት ነበረና” ብዬ የተናገርኩለት ይህ ነው።»
am.R: ዮሐንስ ስለ እርሱ ለሰዎች ተናገረ። እንዲህ ብሎ ጮኸ፦ «ስናገርለት የነበረው ይህ ነው! እንዲህ ብዬ ነበር፦ “ከእኔ በኋላ የሚመጣ አንድ ሰው አለ፤ እርሱ ከእኔ ይበልጣል፤ ከእኔ በፊት ነበረና።”»

hi.L: यूहन्ना उनके विषय में गवाही देता है, और यह कहते हुए पुकार उठा है, "ये वही थे जिनके विषय में मैंने कहा था, 'जो मेरे पीछे आनेवाले हैं, वे मुझसे आगे हो गए हैं, क्योंकि वे मुझसे पहले थे।'"
hi.B: यूहन्ना ने उनके विषय में गवाही दी और पुकारकर कहा, "ये वही हैं जिनके विषय में मैंने कहा था, 'जो मेरे बाद आ रहे हैं, वे मुझसे बढ़कर हैं, क्योंकि वे मुझसे पहले से थे।'"
hi.R: यूहन्ना ने लोगों को उनके बारे में बताया। उसने ज़ोर से पुकारकर कहा, "ये वही हैं जिनकी बात मैं कर रहा था! मैंने कहा था, 'मेरे बाद कोई आ रहे हैं जो मुझसे बड़े हैं, क्योंकि वे मुझसे पहले से मौजूद थे।'"

ru.L: Иоанн свидетельствует о {{deity_pronoun:нём|Нём}} и воскликнул, говоря: «Это был {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}}, о ком я сказал: “Идущий за мной стал впереди меня, потому что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} был прежде меня.”»
ru.B: Иоанн свидетельствовал о {{deity_pronoun:нём|Нём}} и восклицал: «Вот тот, о ком я говорил: “Идущий за мной выше меня, потому что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} был прежде меня.”»
ru.R: Иоанн рассказывал людям о {{deity_pronoun:нём|Нём}}. Он кричал: «Вот о ком я говорил! Я сказал: “После меня придёт тот, кто больше меня, потому что {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} существовал ещё до меня.”»

uk.L: Іван свідчить про {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} і вигукнув, кажучи: «Це був той, про кого я сказав: “Той, хто йде після мене, став попереду мене, бо {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} був раніше за мене.”»
uk.B: Іван свідчив про {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}} і вигукнув: «Це той, про кого я говорив: “Той, хто йде після мене, вищий за мене, бо {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} існував раніше, ніж я.”»
uk.R: Іван розповідав людям про {{deity_pronoun:нього|Нього}}. Він вигукував: «Ось про кого я говорив! Я казав: “Після мене йде той, хто більший за мене, бо {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} існував ще до мене.”»

ja.L: ヨハネはこの方について証しし、叫んで言っている。「この方こそ、わたしが[こう]言った方であった。『わたしの後から来る方は、わたしより先に立つ方となった。わたしより前におられたからである。』」
ja.B: ヨハネはこの方について証しし、声を上げて言った。「この方こそ、わたしが『わたしの後から来る方は、わたしより上に立たれる。わたしより前におられたからだ』と言った方だ。」
ja.R: ヨハネは、この方について証しして、大声で叫びました。「わたしが話していたのは、この方のことだ。わたしは、『わたしの後から来る方は、わたしよりずっと偉い方だ。わたしより前からおられたからだ』と言ったのだ。」

id.L: Yohanes bersaksi tentang {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} dan telah berseru, katanya, "Inilah {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} yang kumaksud ketika aku berkata, 'Dia yang datang sesudah aku telah menjadi lebih utama daripada aku, sebab {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} sudah ada sebelum aku.'"
id.B: Yohanes bersaksi tentang {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} dan berseru, "Dialah yang kumaksudkan ketika aku berkata, 'Dia yang datang sesudah aku lebih tinggi kedudukannya daripada aku, sebab {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} sudah ada sebelum aku.'"
id.R: Yohanes memberi tahu orang-orang tentang {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}}. Dia berseru, "Inilah orang yang kumaksud! Aku pernah berkata, 'Ada yang datang sesudah aku, dan {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} lebih besar daripada aku, sebab {{deity_pronoun:dia|Dia}} sudah ada sebelum aku.'"

John the Baptist was born before Jesus (Luke 1). The claim is that Jesus existed before John, which picks up verses 1-2.
The present and perfect present John's testimony as still standing; English narrative needs the past.

decisions.choice: « » outside, “ ” inside, with the French spacing
decisions.reason: Standard French typography: a no-break space inside « » and before a colon, a narrow one before ! and ?, and “ ” for a quotation within a quotation.

decisions.choice: est placé au-dessus de moi (B); est plus grand que moi (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads rank, not time; "précéder" would suggest time. Literal keeps the spatial "est passé devant moi", which can be read either way, as the Greek can.
"Kumsema mtu" means to speak against someone. "Kusema habari za" (to speak about) is the neutral Swahili.

decisions.choice: John speaks to the crowd in 해라체 ("이분이다"), with honorifics for Jesus ("오시는 분", "계셨기")
decisions.reason: John speaks publicly as a prophet to the people, so the plain style suits him; he speaks of Jesus with the honorific -시- and "분", which shows his respect without changing his speech level.

decisions.choice: historic present "말한다" (L); past (B, R), through this passage
decisions.reason: Korean narrative can use the present for vividness, so Literal keeps John's present tense where the Greek has it ("증언하고 ... 말한다"); Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at L by leaving out "đã" ("Giăng làm chứng")
decisions.reason: Vietnamese marks time with optional words rather than verb endings; Literal leaves out "đã" where the Greek tells a past event in the present, and Balanced and Readable add it where the sense needs it. This holds for the passage.

decisions.choice: historic present kept in Literal ("गवाही देता है")
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present. Literal keeps the present, as the style guide asks; Balanced and Readable use the past (docs/john-terms.md). Noted once for this passage.

decisions.reason: As in Matthew 3:11 and Mark 1:7, John the Baptist speaks of the one who comes after him with respect; John himself is spoken of plainly ("उसने").
John often tells past events in the present. Literal keeps the present, as Russian storytelling also can; Balanced and Readable use the past. This holds through the passage.

decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present (docs/john-terms.md). Literal keeps it so readers see the Greek; Balanced and Readable use the past, which is how Ukrainian narrative runs. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.reason: John tells past events in the present here, as often in the Gospel. Literal keeps the Greek tense; Balanced and Readable narrate in the past, as Japanese narrative does. This holds for the historic presents through the chapter.

decisions.choice: grace upon grace: one gift following another
alternatives: grace in place of grace: the grace in Christ replacing the grace given through the law
decisions.reason: ἀντί usually means "in place of", which supports the alternative and fits verse 17. We chose accumulation because verse 17 does not call the law grace. Literal may keep the open "grace for grace": a level may keep an ambiguity the original has, but may not pick the other side.
No change of meaning, so no footnote.

"Plénitude" is hard for young readers. Readable says what the fullness is by picking up "plein de grâce" from verse 14, and "une grâce après l’autre" keeps the meaning decision: one gift following another.

decisions.choice: utimilifu (L, B); wingi (R); kwa (L); juu ya (B)
decisions.reason: "Utimilifu" is fullness; "ukamilifu" means perfection, which is not the point. Readable says "wingi" (abundance) as the plainer word. Literal translates ἀντὶ word for word as "kwa" (for). Like "grace for grace", "neema kwa neema" can be read as one gift on another or as one gift in place of another, so it keeps the ambiguity the meaning decision leaves open. "Badala ya" (in place of) would pick the alternative reading. Balanced gives the sense in the meaning note, one gift on top of another.

decisions.choice: "은혜 위에 은혜를" (L); "은혜에 은혜를 더하여" (B); "은혜의 선물을 하나 또 하나" (R)
decisions.reason: Every level gives the sense the meaning decision chose, one gift following another (m1). Literal says "은혜 위에 은혜를" (grace upon grace), keeping the short form of the Greek; "은혜를 대신하여" (in place of grace) would pick the reading m1 sets aside, which no level may do. "은혜" is the key term at every level.

decisions.choice: inclusive "chúng ta" (we all, the reader included)
decisions.reason: "We all received" takes in every believer, readers too, so Vietnamese uses the inclusive pronoun here though 1:14 has the eyewitnesses' "chúng tôi".

decisions.choice: "cả ân điển trên ân điển" (L); "hết ân điển này đến ân điển khác" (B); "hết món quà ân điển này đến món quà ân điển khác" (R)
decisions.reason: Every level gives the sense the meaning decision chose, one gift following another (m1). Literal says "ân điển trên ân điển" (grace upon grace), keeping the short form of the Greek; "thay cho" (in place of) would pick the reading m1 sets aside, which no level may do.

decisions.choice: ጸጋን ስለ ጸጋ (grace for grace, L); ጸጋን ከጸጋ በኋላ (grace after grace, B); አንዱን የጸጋ ስጦታ ከሌላው ቀጥሎ (one gift of grace after another, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the open "grace for grace" of the Greek, as meaning decision m1 allows: "ስለ" (for) is as open as the English "for" and does not pick the reading m1 sets aside, as "በጸጋ ፋንታ" (in place of grace) would; a reviewer may prefer another open phrase. Balanced and Readable give the sense of meaning decision m1, one gift following another, with a picture of succession rather than the familiar "upon".
Literal keeps the open "grace for grace" of the Greek, as meaning decision m1 allows; Balanced and Readable give the chosen sense, one gift upon another.
The meaning decision reads the phrase as one gift following another; 'за' says that in ordinary Russian. 'Благодать' is the key term at every level.
Literal renders *anti* by its plain sense "замість"; Balanced gives the sense the meaning decision prefers, one gift following another.
"We all" here are all who have received from his fullness, the readers included, so inclusive "kita", against the eyewitness "kami" of verse 14.

decisions.choice: law and grace side by side, not opposed
decisions.reason: John puts the two clauses side by side with no "but". The law was given, which is also a gift; a contrast word would set law against grace more sharply than John does.
The first time John's Gospel names Jesus. The word is a title, "anointed one" (John 1:41 explains it).
As in English. Spanish writes the name and title as one word, "Jesucristo", so the setting span takes in the name.
After the passive "fut donnée", "par Moïse" would make Moses the giver; the Greek says "through". Readable makes God the subject, so "par Moïse" is clear there.
The first time the Gospel names Jesus. "Christ" is written without the usual hyphen of "Jésus-Christ" so that both options read naturally; the alternative gives the title its meaning.
Swahili has no article, so "Yesu Masihi" reads as naturally as "Yesu Kristo" at every level, where the English needs "the Messiah".
Korean has no article, so the alternative is plain "메시아" where the English has "the Messiah". Both words end in a vowel, so the particle "를" that follows fits either.

decisions.choice: "Đức Giê-xu", with the honorific "Đức" unbracketed at every level
decisions.reason: A revered person's bare name sounds disrespectful in Vietnamese, so "Đức" belongs to how the name is said, not to added meaning, and is not bracketed even at Literal. This holds for the whole book.
After the name the title works as part of it, so it is written without "Đấng"; where it stands alone as a title (1:20) the span is {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}.

decisions.choice: ኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} (Jesus Christ, or Jesus the Messiah)
decisions.reason: Christos is the Greek word for the Hebrew title Messiah, the anointed king. The reader's setting chooses between the familiar "ክርስቶስ" and "መሲሕ", which shows the meaning; Amharic has no article, so both read naturally with the name. This holds for every Christos in John.

decisions.choice: no ግን (but) between the two clauses; ደግሞ (also) at Readable
alternatives: ጸጋና እውነት ግን (but grace and truth)
decisions.reason: The Greek sets the two clauses side by side with no "but", and meaning decision m1 reads law and grace as two gifts, not opposites. Amharic often adds "ግን" here; it is left out, and Readable joins the sentences with "ደግሞ" (also).
"मसीह" is both the familiar name in "यीशु मसीह" and the word Messiah itself, so the choice the English setting offers is already made in Hindi (style guide section 7).
The christos setting, inflected inside each option. 'Мессия' says in Hebrew what 'Христос' says in Greek: the anointed one.
The meaning decision reads Law and grace side by side, not opposed; a Ukrainian "а" would set them against each other.
